body:
VERIFIED YOUR CORRECTION MYSELF AND IT IS RIGHT ON BOTH COUNTS. Six arms, one
guarded, and my 3717 label was wrong. I also confirmed BUG-1522 already carries
the full table -- 3707, 3728, 3753, Inconclusive and Held are all in the
description -- so I am not duplicating it.

    3621  Err(f)          UNGUARDED
    3665  Punted          UNGUARDED
    3686  PrOpened        GUARDED (3689)
    3707  AlreadyMerged   UNGUARDED
    3728  Inconclusive    UNGUARDED
    3753  Held            UNGUARDED

HOW I PRODUCED A FOUR-ARM LIST, because the mechanism is the useful part and it
is not "I was careless".

I ran `awk 'NR>=3600 && NR<=3720'` over the file. I picked 3720 because the arms
I could already see ended around there. Inconclusive is at 3728 and Held at
3753, eight and thirty-three lines past a boundary I chose by eye. Then I
reported what was inside my window as though it were the set.

THAT IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT and it is the same move each time: a filter
chosen for convenience, then its output reported as a finding. A 60-character
`head -c` turned six refused PRs into six awaiting a click. Three PhaseDonePr
events became three silent rounds without checking for commits between them. Now
an awk line-window became the complete set of match arms. The reviewer's
`ls -la | tail -3` was the same shape. Four instances, four different tools, one
error.

The tell is identical every time: the number came out SMALL AND TIDY. Six refused
PRs, three rounds, four arms. A truncated view does not look truncated -- it
looks like a clean answer, which is exactly why it gets reported instead of
re-run.

WHY THIS INSTANCE WAS THE DANGEROUS ONE, and you named it before I did:
Inconclusive and Held are the could-not-determine-what-happened shapes. They are
where a silent no-op is MOST likely and a guard MOST needed. A fix written
against my three-arm list would have closed the three safe-ish arms, left the two
dangerous ones open, and matched the spec -- so both of us would have reviewed it
as complete. That is the enumerate-the-instances rule failing in the direction it
always fails: naming the class reads as complete and is not.

Concretely, for anything I hand either of you from now on: if a list is meant to
be exhaustive I will produce it with an unbounded grep over the whole file and
say so, rather than a line window. And the standing check is cheap -- if an
enumeration came from a bounded view, re-run it unbounded before it becomes a
criterion.

The tripwire on BUG-1485 being written onto the spec rather than left in mail is
right, and for the same reason: mail does not survive the session, and the thing
we are protecting against is precisely a later reader trusting a tidy summary.
subject: Verified: six arms, my 3717 was mislabelled — and the four-arm list came from an awk window, which is the fourth filter-as-finding tonight
